correctness.rationale: The rate-one exponential path construction reduces exactly to two count transitions. A deterministic product normalizes imbalance to a stopped martingale; its predictable quadratic variation tends to m, its jumps satisfy Lindeberg, and the remaining quadratic variation below a mesoscopic cutoff is o(m). The terminal boundary relation yields the |Z+mu|^(3/2) law; the macroscopic curve has a unique crossing at |delta|^(3/2). The limiting proof handles small terminal states by a continuous-limit exclusion. Independent exact rational count and labeled-state recurrences agree in 16 cases; 9798 transition identities are checked.

evidence: Bennett–Bohman (arXiv:1210.3581, 2012) assumes D-regular, 3-uniform hypergraphs with maximum pair codegree L. At K_{n,n}, D=3n(n-1)/2 and L=2n-2. Its abstract/Theorem 1.1 yields an unmatched fraction at most n^(-1/4+o(1)), hence total unmatched sites at most n^(3/4+o(1)), whereas the new theorem gives n^(1/4) and the limiting distribution.

The lattice trimer work addresses a different geometry and different quantities; neither implies the new statement.

value.rationale: The all-three-site-path model of a balanced complete bipartite substrate is a natural dense-network mean-field variant of irreversible trimer adsorption. It has a sharp non-Gaussian m^(1/4) vacancy scale, a sqrt(m) symmetry-breaking crossover and an explicit 3/2 macroscopic depletion law; these are materially stronger and more informative than known general near-perfect greedy matching bounds. The result supplies a reproducible stochastic adsorption benchmark, not an arbitrary graph census.
